drivers.lead: Agostini's eight have stood since 1975, and seven of them came consecutively between 1966 and 1972
drivers.note: Seven straight on MV Agusta, then a two-year gap and an eighth in 1975 on a Yamaha — the only one of his premier-class titles won for another marque. Nobody has won seven in a row since, and only two riders have reached seven at all. The number counted here is the premier class alone: Giacomo Agostini won fifteen world championships in total, the other seven in the 350cc class and most of those in the same seasons as his 500cc ones. Marc Márquez is the reason the record is live again. His seventh came at Motegi in 2025 and put him level with Valentino Rossi, who stopped racing in 2021, which leaves Márquez one title short and the only rider ever to be that close while still on the grid. Six of his seven were won on a Honda; the 2025 one was on a Ducati.

teams.lead: Honda's 25th premier-class constructors' title came in 2019, and it has not won one since
teams.note: The first was in 1966 and the rest arrived in bursts: six straight from 1994 to 1999, four from 2001 to 2004, and four more from 2016 to 2019. No other manufacturer has passed sixteen. MV Agusta has exactly that many, every one of them between 1956 and 1973, and Yamaha has fourteen spread across five decades. What has changed since 2019 is not the record but the present — Ducati has taken six constructors' titles in a row from 2020, on top of a first in 2007, and Honda has added nothing in that time. Seven against twenty-five is no threat to the number, because Ducati would need eighteen more. It is worth remembering, though, that Honda's own second title did not arrive until 1983, seventeen years after its first: these runs stop and start.
